standard.title: Draw conclusions and make proposals
standard.prior_knowledge: From Foundation (AC9HSFS04): Students drew conclusions in response to inquiry questions supported by evidence. From AC9HS1S03: Students interpreted information and compared objects from past and present.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students draw conclusions about continuity and change, how places change, and make proposals for action.

nodes.label: Drawing conclusions about change and place
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use collected information to make conclusions about continuity and change over time and about how places change.
nodes.minimum_width: Draw at least one conclusion about change over time or how a place changes, supported by at least one piece of collected information.
nodes.typical_width: Use collected information from stories, interviews, geographic pictures and comparisons to draw conclusions about: how family roles, occupations or technologies have changed or remained the same; how places change because of seasons or human activity.
wider: Draw conclusions about change in two different contexts (e.g. family roles AND place features) and compare the types of change
Evaluate whether change was positive, negative or mixed, with a reason
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot draw evidence-based conclusions about change, they cannot make meaningful proposals for action — proposals require a conclusion about what is happening or has happened.

response_modes.reason: Model the move from evidence to conclusion explicitly: 'The information shows... so I can conclude that...' Use sentence frames and guided note-taking before expecting independent conclusions.

success_criteria: States at least one conclusion about continuity or change
Supports the conclusion with at least one piece of collected information

nodes.label: Making proposals for action
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe features of a place that is important to them and propose action to care for it or influence a positive future for it.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe one feature of a place that matters to them and propose one specific action to care for it.
nodes.typical_width: Describe features of a personally significant space (classroom, play area, bedroom, beach) and explain what could be done to care for it; imagine how a local feature or place might change in the future and propose action to improve or maintain it.
wider: Develop a plan of action for caring for a specific place, identifying steps and who could help
Imagine two futures for a local place (with and without care) and explain which is preferred and why

response_modes.reason: Proposals integrate place knowledge, significance understanding and evidence-based reasoning into action — the proposal is the integrating output of Year 1 HASS inquiry.

success_criteria: Describes at least one feature of a personally important place
Proposes at least one specific action to care for or improve that place
